findings.reason: the section's whole premise is that the committed copy is the one that travels, so an uncommitted rewrite delivers a repair only the repairing checkout can see; the plan needs the commit step named (through `commit_record_write`, already inside the section's `reckon/crew/review.py` write scope) and a done-when assertion that the rewritten record is committed rather than a modified file.
findings.text: the deliverable stops at "The repair rewrites the record in place", but `repair_run_review` writes with `write_atomically` (`reckon/crew/review.py:3370`) and then calls `store_review`, which writes only the host staging path under `review_store_root`; the committed tree is git-tracked and the sibling committed-write path commits through `commit_record_write` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:302-329`) precisely because an uncommitted tracked write "sits as a modified file the next reader would trip on" — so a node built to this text leaves the repair in the project checkout uncommitted, where no other clone reads it, while the done-when (which reads the file from disk) cannot detect the difference

findings.reason: a worker building the single-record fixture the section's singular "a record in the committed location" describes gets the stated result unchanged; the gap only bites a fixture copied from a sibling section, and one clause ("at a head holding only this record") would remove it.
findings.text: the first case asserts `select_review_for_head` returns the repaired record reading `unparsed` "afterwards", but with §25 landed the committed selection prefers a parsed, complete record over any other at the same head (`reckon/crew/review_records.py` `_select_stored_record`), so the assertion holds only if the fixture's committed run directory holds the repaired record alone — a precondition the section does not state, and one a worker reusing §25's two-record fixture would violate

response_events.note: §26 now commits the repaired committed record through commit_record_write, as the sibling committed write does, and grants reckon/crew/review_records.py
